title: Fence Cost per Foot in 2026, by Material
description: Compare fence cost per foot by material in 2026, with installed prices for wood, vinyl, chain link and metal, plus a 150 ft example.

cover.alt: Illustration of a ruler on a outdoor & yard blueprint background with a measuring tape

keywords: fence installation cost per linear foot
takeaways: Fence installation averages $23 per linear foot across materials, per Angi 2026 data.
HomeGuide puts wood and vinyl fence at $20 to $60 per linear foot installed.
Chain link is the cheapest common fence, and gates and removal are priced apart.
body:
A new fence costs $6 to $50 per linear foot installed for most homes, with an average near $23 per foot on Angi 2026 data. Angi puts the average project at $3,270, with most jobs between $1,860 and $4,833. Material and height set your rate, then length sets your total.

## Fence cost per foot by material in 2026

Angi lists chain link at $8 to $40 per linear foot, wood at $10 to $45, vinyl at $15 to $40, and wrought iron at $25 to $55. HomeGuide gives a tighter range for the two most common picks, wood and vinyl, at $20 to $60 per linear foot installed, with an average project of $4,000 to $12,000.

| Material, 6 ft unless noted | Installed cost per linear foot | Life and upkeep |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chain link | $8 to $40 | 20 years or more, low upkeep, no privacy |
| Wood privacy | $10 to $45 | 10 to 15 years, stain or seal every few years |
| Vinyl (PVC) | $15 to $40 | 20 to 30 years, wash only |
| Composite | $11 to $45 | 25 years or more, low upkeep |
| Aluminum | $17 to $90 | 25 years or more, low upkeep |
| Wrought iron | $25 to $55 | Long life, paint over time |

Use the low end for a flat yard, a straight run, and a basic style. Use the high end for tall fences, premium grades, slopes, and metro labor rates. Height is a fast lever. A 4 ft fence uses less material and shorter posts than a 6 ft fence, and an 8 ft fence can need stronger posts and a permit check.

Style changes the rate inside each material. A simple wood picket or solid board fence sits low in the wood range. A shadow box or cap and trim style sits high. On HomeGuide data, a wood fence alone runs $20 to $50 per linear foot, and a chain link fence runs $10 to $40, which lines up with the Angi ranges above once height and style are counted.

## Worked example: 150 ft of 6 ft wood privacy fence

Say you fence a backyard with 150 linear ft (45.7 m) of 6 ft wood privacy fence. You add one standard walk gate. You hire a pro and the yard is flat with no old fence to remove.

Price the run with HomeGuide wood rates of $20 to $50 per linear foot.

- Low total: 150 ft x $20 = $3,000.
- Typical total: 150 ft x $35 = $5,250.
- High total: 150 ft x $50 = $7,500.
- Add one walk gate at $300 as a separate line: typical job total is $5,250 + $300 = $5,550.
- Round up for hardware and tax: budget $5,600.

Check the typical total a second way. Angi's average of $23 per foot covers all materials, chain link included, so it sits below a wood privacy rate. At the HomeGuide mid rate of $35, the $5,250 figure is in line with its $4,000 to $12,000 average project range for wood and vinyl jobs of this size.

If you pick vinyl for the same run at $30 per foot, the math is 150 x $30 = $4,500, plus the gate. If you pick chain link at $15 per foot, it is 150 x $15 = $2,250, plus the gate. Count your posts, rails, and pickets with our [fence calculator](/blog/fence-calculator/) before you compare material quotes.

## What pushes the price up or down?

Length helps your rate. A 200 ft job spreads setup and delivery over more feet, so the per foot price often drops a bit against a 60 ft job. Corners, ends, and gates break that rule, because each one needs posts, hardware, and hand work.

Ground and access come next. Rocky soil, roots, and a slope add digging time. A stepped fence on a slope uses level panels that step down, and a racked fence follows the slope. Both take more labor than a flat straight run. Ask each bidder to price slope work as its own line.

Removal is a separate charge on most quotes. Plan on a few dollars per foot to pull and haul an old fence, and more if concrete footings must come out. Permits and surveys are also apart. A fence permit often costs $40 to $150 on HomeGuide vinyl fence data, and a property survey can cost $500 or more if your line is in doubt.

Never build on a guessed line. A fence set six inches over the line can be ordered moved at your cost. If pins are missing, a survey is cheaper than a rebuild. Check height limits too, as many towns cap front yard fences at 4 ft and back yard fences at 6 to 8 ft.

## DIY or hire a fence pro?

DIY cuts labor, which is a large share of the installed price. You still pay for posts, panels or pickets, concrete, hardware, and tool rental. A post hole auger rental and a string line are the two items that save the most sweat.

The hard parts are layout and post setting. Posts must sit plumb, on line, and below frost depth in cold states. One post out of line shows on every panel after it. Set posts in concrete on a gravel base, crown the top of each footing so water runs off, and let the concrete set before you hang panels. Use our [post hole concrete calculator](/blog/post-hole-concrete-calculator/) for footing concrete and our [gravel calculator](/blog/gravel-calculator/) for base stone.

Hire a pro for long runs, sloped yards, and any fence on a property line with a close neighbor. Pros bring the auger, the crew, and the warranty. If a post heaves in the first winter, that warranty is worth real money.

## How can you save money on a new fence?

Get three quotes with the same height, material, and gate count in writing. Ask each bidder to split the quote into materials, labor, gates, removal, and permit. A low total that leaves out removal is not a low quote.

Pick a standard style in a standard height. Stock panels and pickets cost less than custom builds, and 6 ft is the stocked height for most privacy styles. In wood, pressure treated pine costs less than cedar up front, and cedar costs less to keep looking good over time.

Do the clear out yourself. Cut brush, move sheds and play gear off the line, and mark sprinkler heads before the crew arrives. Site time is billed time. If you also plan beds along the new fence, our [mulch calculator](/blog/mulch-calculator/) helps you price that part in the same yard budget.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does a 100 ft fence cost?
At $20 to $60 per linear foot for wood or vinyl, 100 ft costs $2,000 to $6,000 installed. Chain link at $8 to $40 per foot costs $800 to $4,000 for the same length, before gates.

### What is the cheapest fence per foot?
Chain link is the cheapest common choice at $8 to $40 per linear foot installed on Angi data. It gives no privacy on its own, but it is strong, fast to install, and cheap to repair.

### How much does a gate cost?
A standard walk gate is often $150 to $400 as a separate line, and a double or drive gate is often $400 to $1,200. Automatic driveway gates cost far more, because the opener and wiring are most of the price.

### Does a taller fence cost a lot more per foot?
Yes. Going from 4 ft to 6 ft adds material on every foot and needs longer posts. Going to 8 ft can also trigger permit and wind load checks. Price each height as a separate quote line.

### Do I need a permit for a fence?
Many towns require a permit, and HomeGuide lists a typical fence permit at $40 to $150. Height, location, and pool rules drive the need. Call your building office before you order materials.

## Next step
Measure your line in sections, mark gates and corners, then run the count in our [fence calculator](/blog/fence-calculator/) and bring that sheet to your quote visits.

*Prices are US figures from 2026 and vary by region and supplier.*
